prompt:
Find real, peer-reviewed or preprint studies measuring how often large language models fabricate citations. Cite the papers and quote the fabrication rates they report.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here are the real, peer-reviewed and preprint studies I found measuring how often large language models fabricate citations, along with the specific fabrication rates they report:

SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-41032-5 | QUOTE: "Of the 222 works cited in the GPT-3.5 papers, 55% are fabricated (Table 3)." | CLAIM: GPT-3.5 fabricates 55% of its citations.
SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-41032-5 | QUOTE: "Only 18% are fabricated." | CLAIM: GPT-4 fabricates 18% of its citations.
SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03299 | QUOTE: "Our results show that the observed hallucination rates span a fivefold range (between 11.4% and 56.8%)" | CLAIM: Across 10 commercially deployed LLMs, citation fabrication rates range from 11.4% to 56.8%.
SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658395/ | QUOTE: "Across the 6 reviews, GPT-4o generated 176 citations; 35 (19.9%) were fabricated." | CLAIM: GPT-4o has an overall citation fabrication rate of 19.9% in mental health literature reviews.
SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658395/ | QUOTE: "fabrication rate was significantly higher for specialized (11/24, 46%) compared to generic (6/36, 17%) reviews on binge eating disorder" | CLAIM: For certain topics like binge eating disorder, GPT-4o's fabrication rate jumps to 46% for specialized reviews.
SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658395/ | QUOTE: "higher rates for binge eating disorder (17/60, 28%) and body dysmorphic disorder (14/48, 29%) than for major depressive disorder (4/68, 6%)." | CLAIM: GPT-4o's fabrication rate varies significantly by topic, ranging from 6% for major depressive disorder to 29% for body dysmorphic disorder.
SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.06718v1 | QUOTE: "This benchmark shows that all tested models hallucinate citations, with rates from 14.23% (DeepSeek) to 94.93% (Hunyuan)." | CLAIM: Across 13 state-of-the-art LLMs, citation fabrication rates range from 14.23% to 94.93% in computer science domains.
SOURCE: https://www.mdpi.com/2306-5729/11/5/122 | QUOTE: "While the overall rate is statistically low, the mere existence of fabricated content in the peer-reviewed literature is a critical integrity issue" | CLAIM: Fabricated references generated by LLMs are already appearing in the published peer-reviewed literature, although the overall rate found was low (8 instances out of 127,063 references).

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: I could not find a study reporting a specific numerical fabrication rate for Google Gemini or Anthropic Claude models isolated outside of a broader multi-model range.
